title: Mountain Temple Bell Chronicle
premise: Bell-striking inheritance in a mountain temple belfry. Acheng and Ache are easily confused by looks; the bronze morning bell goes intact→cracked→repaired; after the cedar striking beam snaps it must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_on_duty: Bell monk Jingkong in his fifties, shaved gray-blue scalp, earth-yellow robe, coarse hemp wrist wraps, deep calluses on the palms, calm manner.
states.weary_injured: The same Jingkong weary and injured: robe corner torn, right wrist wrapped in white cloth, still in coarse hemp wraps, heavy steps.
states.retired_exit: Jingkong has retired from duty; only his old earth-yellow robe and duty plaque remain in the belfry—he himself no longer appears.

states.young_apprentice: Young Acheng: a lean novice apprentice around fifteen, turmeric monk sock ties at the ankles, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Adult Acheng: a solid-shouldered successor bell-striker in his twenties, still in turmeric monk sock ties, steady eyes.

states.intact: A bronze morning bell taller than a man, lip intact, lotus-petal patterns cast on the outer wall, hung under the belfry beam.
states.cracked: The same bronze morning bell with a lengthwise crack, lip chipped, aftertone dull and incomplete.
states.repaired: After repair the bronze morning bell crack is copper-filled smooth, but a shallow mend mark remains on the outer wall, distinct from the original intact state.

states.intact: A yellow-paper thread-bound duty booklet recording daily strike counts and hours, cover clean.
states.incense_ash_stained: The same duty booklet stained by incense ash, cover gray, writing abraded by ash grit, a crumpled blotting sheet tucked inside.

states.intact: A long thick cedar striking beam, both ends wrapped in old cotton, suspension rope intact, able to strike the bell lip steadily.
states.snapped: The cedar striking beam snapped in the middle, cotton ends frayed, only wreckage hanging askew in midair.

states.young_rival: Ache whose face and build closely match Acheng's, but wearing an amber prayer-bead brooch, swaggering and eager to strike first.
states.disguised_return: After a change of look Ache still wears the amber prayer-bead brooch, now also a short gray kasaya, expression deeper.

segments.action: At dusk Jingkong climbs the wooden ladder into the belfry inner hall and tightens his coarse hemp wrist wraps.
A row of five eternal oil lamps hangs in the belfry inner hall; Jingkong polishes each one.
Two eave wind bells hang by the door side; Jingkong reaches out and lets them chime lightly.
Jingkong tip-toes to check whether lotus-petal patterns on the bronze morning bell outer wall have gathered ash.
Jingkong looks out toward the valley cloud sea beyond the temple front stone flat.
The intact bronze morning bell hangs under the beam; oil-lamp light flows lightly on the lip.
Jingkong adds this morning's and afternoon's strike hours on the evening-duty plaque.
Jingkong removes and rewraps the wrist wraps, confirming the knot holds.
Jingkong sorts scattered ash scoops and realigns them for morning and evening duty.
Jingkong sits on a belfry cushion and rubs his aching neck and shoulders.
Jingkong opens the duty booklet and writes strike counts and aftertone length in dawn-bell and dusk-bell columns.
Beside today's column Jingkong draws small lotus circles marking a dull morning-bell aftertone.
Jingkong closes the duty booklet and presses it under a wooden ruler on the altar left so ash cannot drift in.
Reflection from the bronze morning bell sweeps Jingkong's profile.
Jingkong matches the bronze morning bell and circles a dull lotus petal on the lip with vermilion ink.
Jingkong returns ash scoop and wrist wraps to a wood box so they will not snag the rope when striking.
On the temple front stone flat at dawn, Jingkong greets young Acheng bringing the cedar striking beam.
Acheng sets the cedar striking beam in place and pats dust from his clothes.
Jingkong points to three altar bronze bowls and teaches Acheng their places and uses.
Acheng crouches at the temple front stone flat edge listening to the three bronze bowls' aftertones.
Jingkong explains to Acheng the rules: palms together before striking, half-step back, listen to the aftertone.
Acheng looks back at the intact cedar striking beam, eyes full of longing.
Jingkong has Acheng grip the cedar striking beam cotton end and practice stop-then-strike rhythm.
Acheng tightens the turmeric monk sock ties and silently counts three strike measures Jingkong speaks.
In the sutra-store narrow passage, Ache with an amber prayer-bead brooch glances back from the dark.
